what_its_for: Piroxicam is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to relieve pain, swelling, stiffness, and tenderness caused by arthritis, including osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. It helps reduce inflammation in your joints so you can move more comfortably.
how_to_take: Take piroxicam exactly as your doctor prescribed. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water (8 ounces). Take it with food, milk, or an antacid to help prevent stomach upset. Stay upright (do not lie down) for at least 10 minutes after taking it. Take it at the same time every day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 20 mg taken once a day, or your doctor may split it into 10 mg twice a day. Do not take more than 20 mg in one day unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store piroxicam capsules at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep them away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist about medication take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking piroxicam, as it increases your risk of stomach bleeding. Do not take other NSAIDs (such as ibuprofen, naproxen, or aspirin for pain) at the same time unless your doctor approves. Avoid smoking, which can also worsen stomach problems. Do not take more than the recommended dose. Tell your dentist or surgeon that you take this medication before any procedure, as it can affect bleeding.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you notice: black, tarry, or bloody stools; vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds; severe stomach pain; chest pain, shortness of breath, sudden weakness, or slurred speech (signs of a heart attack or stroke); swelling of your face, lips, throat, or tongue (allergic reaction); yellowing of your skin or eyes (liver problems); unusual weight gain or swelling in your legs; or little to no urination (kidney problems). Also contact your doctor if your pain is not improving after a few weeks.
when_it_works: Piroxicam may start to relieve some pain and stiffness within the first few days, but it usually takes 1 to 2 weeks of regular use to feel the full benefit. Some people with arthritis may need up to 2 weeks before noticing significant improvement. Be patient and keep taking it as directed.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Use with extra caution, as you are at higher risk for stomach bleeding, kidney problems, and fluid retention. Your doctor may prescribe a lower dose or monitor you more closely. Pregnancy: Do not use piroxicam during the last 3 months (third trimester) of pregnancy, as it can harm the unborn baby. Talk to your doctor before using it in early pregnancy. Breastfeeding: Piroxicam passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while on this medication. Children: Piroxicam is generally not recommended for children. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as piroxicam may not be safe for you or may require dose adjustments.
